summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.16/609)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni i badle ʕam u ḥyoṭayḏa mikalfowa b 15-20 noṭat.
data.translation: That is, a suit together with its tailoring used to cost 15–20 notes.

rationale: New Infectum-wa cost cell; price with b- and feminine suit subject. mi- alone is not a Detransitive marker.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.48/2125)

data.translation: Even if they had offered it to me, I would not have agreed.

rationale: New Infectum-wa commissioning cell, counterfactual scope; segmentation is provisional and queried.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.7/1842)

data.turoyo: U nošo, d mkalafwole ste, d huwewo əmkan b iḏe, samwo ṭalab dan noše.
data.translation: And anyone who asked him, if he had the means in his hand, he would fulfil people's request.

rationale: New Infectum-wa sense-1 cell; human requester and recipient plus explicit ṭalab show nonbinding requests.

summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (Jan 2.10/2710)

data.turoyo: W mkamelan, bəṯər, annaqla umarno: "B əšme d sayyidna u faṭəryarxo, b əšme d kulan di ǧamaʕ w dak kuhne ʕəmum dad dayfe, sidayna lu muklo mkalfe ne."
data.translation: And we finished. Afterwards, then I say: 'In the name of Sayyidna the patriarch, in the name of all of us, of the congregation and the priests, all the guests are invited to our place for a meal.'

rationale: First unambiguous Detransitive state: plural mkalfe ne with guests as subjects and meal goal.

summary: New sense 3b: (mit l-) jemandem ein Angebot machen, etwas anbieten

data.label: 3b
data.gloss: (mit l-) jemandem ein Angebot machen, etwas anbieten

rationale: Two institutional-agent passages concern an offer of pension/support or continued residence, expressed by hawxa mede/hawxa and recipient suffixes; this is more than presenting speech, and does not impose a task.

summary: New sense 1: (mit l-) zu etwas eingeladen sein (Detrans.)
rationale: Plural mkalfe ne has all guests as subjects and lu muklo as the invitation goal; attendance at a meal is not a binding commission. One explicit token suffices; ambiguous mkalaffe is not used to establish this sense.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (JTM 1.3/5)

data.turoyo: Haṯe ləġġe darəǧ yo, kul nošo kuḏaʕla, məd mərre "rḥəmanxu, kubʕena d ruḥmitullan", kuḏʕi b ruḥayye, d kətte kaččəke, w kuḏʕi lani, d kəmkalfənne u medano, kətte xort, lašan ṭlobo aṯən.
data.translation: Das ist eine gängige Ausdrucksweise, die jeder versteht. Wenn sie sagen: Wir haben euch liebgewonnen, und wir möchten, dass auch ihr uns liebgewinnt, dann verstehen (die Eltern), dass sie ein Mädchen haben, und dass diejenigen, die ihnen dieses Angebot machen, einen junge Mann haben und dass sie zwecks Brautwerbung gekommen sind.

rationale: First Infectum-3 example: overt proposal object and recipient suffix extend the already numbered vortragen sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 3.2/18)

data.turoyo: <...> Manṭela mkalafla ʕal u ṣulḥ, w qayəm aṯi w ǧġil ʕam aʕ ʕəwardnoye <...>
data.translation: Sie brachte ihn und beauftragte ihn, Frieden zu stiften. Er machte sich auf, kam und redete mit den Leuten von ʿIwardo.

rationale: Thin Preterit 1; assigned task with ʕal u ṣulḥ.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (91/25)

data.turoyo: Mkalafli aḥ ḥawronayḏi, məlli: “Hatu hwawu qaršə dəṯṯe w mḥarebu aʕmayye w ono bi ḥila gməfrašno mənxu w me bəṯrayye da gdoṯeno, bu šalfo gqoṭanno ḥa mənne <...>
data.translation: Ich schlug meinen Kameraden vor: Bleibt ihr ihnen gegenüberstehen und kämpft mit ihnen, ich werde mich heimlich von euch trennen, von hinten an sie herankommen und einen von ihnen mit dem Messer töten.

rationale: Thin Preterit 1; first-person commissioning with human object and task quotation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 1.48/2124)

data.turoyo: yawmo mede nošo man noše di dawle lə mkaləflelox: “Tox hway xəfya, tox hway flan...“ Lə mərallox?
data.translation: one day, something, someone among the state's people did not commission you, “Come, become an informer; come, become such-and-such...” Didn't they tell you?

rationale: Round-1 Preterit 1 has four examples; explicit singular L-agent plus addressee and task quotation fills to five.

summary: example for sense 3b in Preterit (Jan 3.40/1147)

data.turoyo: Hawxa mede i dawle d Kamal w lay yatume d Kamal lə mkaləfallox?
data.translation: Did the state of Kemal and the orphans of Kemal not offer you anything like that?

rationale: New offer subsense; institutional plural agent and recipient -lox.

summary: example for sense 3b in Preterit (Jan 3.40/1149)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni hawxa lə mkaləflalox, yaʕni, hat lə mərallox: "Kḥaqlox hawxa w fəš harke."
data.translation: That is, did it not make you an offer like that, that is, did they not say to you: "It is your due, like this, and stay here."

rationale: Second new 3b example; feminine state agent -la and addressee -lox with explicit proposed benefit/stay.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Jan 2.12/2941)

data.turoyo: Hul d ksoyəm ruḥe kar w hul d ksoyəm at tadarək du darbo, d oṯe hul l harke, kmikalfo aʕle b ġalabe.
data.translation: By the time a person gets himself ready and makes the preparations for the journey, to come all the way here, it costs him a great deal.

rationale: Thin cost Infectum cell; explicit ʕal- cost bearer and b- amount.

summary: The current sense inventory covers every lexical use: a person with an imposed task (1), cost (2), or a presented speech/proposal with recipient (3). JTM 1.3/5 has a proposal as object, so no marriage-specific sense is needed.

Task coding varies between an overt person plus d-clause, a fronted nominal task, and ʕal u ṣulḥ. German vorschlagen in 91/25 does not by itself overturn the instruction reading of the direct task quotation.

49/24 clearly concerns cost borne by -lan, but its spelling mkalaflan is identical to the first-person plural commissioning form at 35/46. The lookup form only confirms that inherited homograph; it does not prove the cost token’s box.

57/139 contains the Arabic formula law mahma kallaf ilʔamr. It documents contact/code-switching, not a new Turoyo stem or a secure Turoyo Preterit. No new phrase is published solely from this switched clause.
Permitted lookups: search kallaf (no hits) and form mkalaflan (existing Preterit under klf).
All 20 occurrences receive a decision. Round-1 proposals are retained as baseline only; no repeated active sense or correction is serialized.
New Detransitive invitation state is restricted to mkalfe ne with overt plural subjects and lu muklo. Earlier mkalaffe tokens remain unresolved; no example is published from them.

The offer subsense 3b specialises presentation of a proposal and is supported by two adjacent, independently formulated questions. It does not renumber inherited 1–3 or infer acceptance of the offered benefit.

mkalfiwoli is provisionally Infectum-wa (-i-wo-li), with recipient -li. English had offered does not prove Preterit-wa. The clear contrast between mkaləf-le-lox and mkaləf-la-lox demonstrates agent versus recipient coding.
mikalfowa/kmikalfo in cost clauses have variant vowels but no mi-t- morphology. Cost-bearer ʕal- and price/amount b- belong in research notes without rewriting inherited kosten.
English quotations are supplied machine translations. Commissioning, requesting, offering and invitation judgments are grounded in task quotations, ṭalab, hawxa mede and lu muklo.
At 49/24 is mkalaflan a prospective-concessive Preterit with affected payer, or an Infectum with payer suffix? A paradigm/recording is needed before boxing it.
Should the Arabic formula at 57/139 be retained as a contact note only, or separately documented as an adopted phrase?
Does mkalafli in 91/25 imply a binding assignment or a proposed plan in this setting? Current sense 1 is retained because the task is explicitly imposed on the companions.
Confirm mkalfiwoli at Jan 1.48/2125 as plural Infectum-wa with recipient -li; if Preterit-wa, identify the agent suffix independently.
Resolve mkalaffe at Jan 1.48/2129, 2131 and Jan 2.5/1509: finite compressed form or a state predicate? These do not establish an additional Detransitive commissioning sense.
Is mkalfe ne lu muklo the usual formula for invited to a meal, and does its active counterpart use ordinary sense 1 or a distinct invitation sense?
Confirm mi- vowels of the active cost predicate and ʕal- coding of the cost bearer in Jan 2.12/2941.
Do the offer passages at Jan 3.40/1147–1149 specifically offer a pension or a continued-residence arrangement? The subsense is kept broader than either particular benefit.
Commissioning ranges from official recruitment to ritual roles and requests for help; refusal shows that these need not entail compliance. No recruitment-specific sense is added.
Cost has a commodity or journey/preparation as subject, b- price/amount and ʕal- cost bearer. This supplies argument coding missing from the inherited single cost example.
